title: Deck Staining in Ocala, FL | Strip, Repair, Re-Stain
description: Deck staining in Ocala, FL: failed coatings stripped, soft boards replaced, and penetrating stain sprayed and back-brushed on decks, stairs, and pergolas.
h1: Deck Staining in Ocala, FL That Soaks In Instead of Peeling Off
heroIntro: A deck in Ocala sits in direct sun, takes summer downpours, and stays damp in shaded corners. We strip what has failed, fix soft boards, and use stain that penetrates the wood.

sections.h2: Why Ocala decks fail where they do
body: Deck finishes rarely fail evenly. The open middle of the deck takes the full afternoon sun and turns gray first, while the edges under eaves or trees stay damp after storms and grow mildew. Stair treads and the path to the door wear through from foot traffic. On equestrian properties in SW and NW Ocala, large decks and pergolas often sit fully exposed, which speeds all of that up. Deck staining in Ocala, FL has to address each zone, not just recoat the top.
If you are unsure whether boards are still sound, our article on signs of deck wood rot explains what to check before calling.

Film-forming coatings that have started to peel must come off, because new stain cannot soak through them. We strip failed finish, wash and treat mildew, and sand the surface so it accepts stain evenly. Soft or split boards and loose hardware are replaced or fixed as listed on the estimate.

We then apply penetrating stain, sprayed and back-brushed so it works into the grain rather than sitting on top. Stain needs dry wood, so we schedule application after the wood has had time to dry following the wash, and we watch the forecast during summer.

Masking is part of the job too. Siding next to the deck, door thresholds, screens, plantings, and patio furniture are covered before any stripper or stain is applied, and the area is rinsed and cleaned before the crew leaves each day.
bullets: Deck surface, rails, balusters, and stairs
Pergolas and other attached wood structures
Transparent, semi-transparent, or solid stain options

body: Transparent stain shows the most grain but gives the least UV protection, so on a fully exposed deck it fades quickest. Semi-transparent balances grain and protection and suits most Ocala decks. Solid stain hides mismatched boards and repairs well and blocks the most sun, but it behaves more like a coating and needs care on walking surfaces. We show samples on your own boards before you choose.

Deck work fits best in the October through May window, when dry stretches are longer. Once approved, the deck usually goes on the calendar within one to three weeks. Owners often stain the deck and the fence in one visit through our Ocala fence painting and staining, and many begin with soft washing of the house at the same time. faqs.q: How often does a deck need restaining in Ocala?
faqs.a: It depends on sun exposure, stain opacity, and traffic. Fully exposed decks with transparent stain need attention soonest. We look at your deck's condition at the walkthrough and explain what we see.

faqs.q: Can you stain over my deck's old peeling finish?
faqs.a: No. Peeling film blocks new stain from penetrating, so failed coatings are stripped and the wood is sanded first.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted deck boards?
faqs.a: Yes. Board replacement and hardware fixes are listed on the written estimate based on what we find during the walkthrough.

faqs.q: Can my Ocala deck and pergola be stained the same color?
faqs.a: Yes. We apply the same stain system to the deck, rails, stairs, and pergola so the color and wear pattern stay consistent across the whole structure.
